title: Alma’s people flee into the wilderness
summary: Warned by the Lord that King Noah’s armies would come, Alma makes this known to his people. They gather their flocks and grain and depart into the wilderness before the armies. The Lord strengthens them so the people of King Noah cannot overtake them to destroy them. They flee eight days’ journey into the wilderness.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord warns Alma that King Noah’s armies will come upon them, and Alma makes this known to his people.
The people gather their flocks, take grain, and depart into the wilderness before King Noah’s armies.
The Lord strengthens them, and the people of King Noah cannot overtake them to destroy them.
They flee eight days’ journey into the wilderness.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma’s people travel with flocks and grain.
unspecified_visual_details: The travelers’ clothing, ages, and number.
The wilderness terrain and weather.

narration.text: Now Alma, having been warned of the Lord that the armies of king Noah would come upon them, and having made it known to his people,
they gathered together their flocks, and took of their grain, and departed into the wilderness before the armies of king Noah.
And they fled eight days’ journey into the wilderness.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage attributes the escape to the Lord’s strengthening but describes no visible divine appearance or intervention.
prohibited_inventions: Inventing Alma’s words to his people.
Depicting a visible divine appearance or supernatural intervention.
Showing King Noah’s armies overtaking the fleeing people.

title: The people ask Alma to be king
summary: The people want Alma as their king because they love him. Alma teaches against esteeming one person above another and says having a king would be well if they could always have just kings.

explicit_facts.text: The people desire Alma as king because he is beloved by them.
Alma says it is not expedient to have a king and teaches that one person should not be esteemed above another.
Alma says having a king would be well if they could always have just men as kings.

title: Alma recalls his repentance

Alma says he is unworthy to glory of himself.

title: Stand fast in liberty
summary: Alma says the people were oppressed and brought into iniquity by Noah and his priests, but delivered from bondage. He urges them to stand fast in liberty and trust only a godly teacher or minister.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says the people were oppressed and in bondage to Noah and his priests, who brought them into iniquity.
Alma says God delivered them from Noah's people and from the bonds of iniquity, and urges them to stand fast in liberty and not trust a man as king.
Alma says not to trust a teacher or minister unless the person is of God, walks in God's ways, and keeps his commandments.

unspecified_visual_details: Any physical representation of bondage or deliverance.
